method: Independent exact-export review of actual full-resolution images, primary morphology references, decoded geometry, raw automated reports and recovered target-renderer CI evidence. Scope and limitations are stated below.
observations: Independently consulted American Fern Society, Jerald Pinson, About Ferns: Shared, Derived Traits, Figure 2 and adjacent morphology paragraphs, and NHM Unfurl the secrets of ferns: Going underground, What ferns did dinosaurs eat? and The remarkable life cycle of ferns. No reference media or text was incorporated.

Visible botanical hierarchy is consistent with the limited concept: one low crown, bare stipes continuing into curved rachises, first-division pinnae attached on either side, and one continuous young coiled frond. These are broad morphology obligations; pinna shape, count, arrangement, palette and dimensions remain artistic choices.

No flowers or seeds are modeled or claimed. Spore structures and microscopic/internal anatomy are not depicted. The simplified crown is an above-ground attachment concept, not a detailed rhizome/root-system reconstruction.

Both sources distinguish the age of the fern group from the identity of living species. This asset claims no named modern/fossil taxon, ancient locality or measured specimen. The brief’s evidence-informed stylized fern concept wording is appropriate; Mesozoic ecological compatibility and species-level accuracy remain unclaimed.
